**Synopsis:**
The RBI announced an open market bond sale (OMO) of ₹1 trillion (~$10.5B) across three tranches between Sept 16–28 to drain excess rupee liquidity, which has been flooding the banking system following a massive $127B FX mobilisation scheme. Overnight rates have slid below the monetary policy corridor floor, and elevated oil prices add inflationary risk. Markets are concerned the OMO sales will push government borrowing costs higher, with the 10-year yield already up 26bps in four weeks. Some analysts preferred CRR hikes over OMO sales as a less disruptive tool.
